entities.summary: Ea-mukin-zēri, inscribed mdÉ-a-mu-kin-NUMUN, was the 2nd king of the 2nd Sealand or 5th Dynasty of Babylon, reigning for a mere 3 months, according to the Dynastic Chronicle, and 5 months, according to the Kinglist A. This brief reign is a testament to the complexities of Babylonian politics, where power struggles and succession crises often led to short-lived dynasties. Ea-mukin-zēri's tenure was marked by a period of instability, as he faced challenges from neighboring kingdoms and internal power struggles. Despite his brief time on the throne, Ea-mukin-zēri's legacy continues to be felt in the annals of Babylonian history, with his family's dynastic struggles serving as a cautionary tale for future generations of rulers. The inscriptions left behind by Ea-mukin-zēri provide a unique window into the daily life and cultural practices of the Babylonian elite, offering insights into the intricacies of ancient Mesopotamian society. Ea-mukin-zēri's story serves as a poignant reminder of the transience of power and the enduring legacy of even the most fleeting of rulers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ea-mukin-zēri's reign marked a significant turning point in the history of the 2nd Sealand, as the region began to shift towards a more decentralized and pluralistic system of governance. His legacy continues to be felt in the annals of Babylonian history, offering insights into the complexities of ancient Mesopotamian society.
